messages:
eli: Heads up — Acme reported 503s + huge tail latency since 06:12 UTC. They also saw requests land in APAC even though their app is EU-only. Customer saw a billing spike. Can someone pick this up?

anna: dropping the customer convo link: https://acme.example/incident-987 — they pasted an `X-Request-Id` and some response headers.

jonas: I'm on call, grabbing logs for their request id `req_0a9c1f2b`. Quick check: is there a recent capacity event in eu-west?

maria: Confirmed: between 06:10–06:15 there was a transient capacity exhaustion on the eu-west model pool (gpu-pool-eu-8). Autoscaler hit a cooldown and requests started being routed elsewhere. Router metrics show a surge of "auto-relocate" decisions from eu-west -> apac-1.

eli: The customer says when requests hit APAC they get 401s: token audience / scope mismatch. Looks like the router didn't re-scope tokens for the target region.

jonas: Repro locally with their header. Using curl against our public endpoint produced the same region hop:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer x.x.x" -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west" https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate
```

Response headers from my run: `X-Routed-Region: apac-1`, `X-Server-Queue: 42`, `X-Request-Id: req_0a9c1f2b` and body `{"error":"401 unauthorized"}`.

maria: Router logs show policy decision: preferred_region=eu-west, fallback_region=apac-1 because eu-west queue_depth > 1000 and capacity_util >= 99. But we didn't attach `target_token_audience` when relocating, so the auth layer rejects.

eli: That explains the 401s. Billing team — see `billing-bot` below: cross-region egress recorded as ~120GB in 06:10–06:20 window for this tenant.

billing-bot: Detected unusual cross-region egress for tenant `acme` — 121.4GB forwarded from eu-west -> apac-1 between 2025-11-22T06:10:00Z and 2025-11-22T06:20:00Z. Potential charge: $12.30 (preview).

anna: Customer is asking for root cause and a mitigation they can apply now. Can we provide repro steps and an immediate workaround?

maria: Root cause summary (short): autoscaler cooldown + sudden queueing in eu-west triggered router auto-relocate to apac-1. Router relocation did not translate token audience/scope for relocated requests -> 401s. Secondary effect: cross-region egress billing spike.

jonas: Immediate mitigations:
- patch router-policy to include `target_token_audience` during relocate (hotfix queued).
- temporary sticky-hint: customers can set header `X-Prefer-Region: eu-west` to force sticky routing until pool recovers.
- increase eu-west reserved capacity or pop a short warmup scale to absorb burst.

eli: Can you add concrete repro steps so support can show customer?

maria: Repro steps for support:
1) Use the customer's API key and reproduce with `X-Client-Region: eu-west` header.
2) Watch `X-Routed-Region` response header to confirm hop.
3) If hop occurs, confirm 401 and capture full response headers+request id.
4) From infra: `kubectl logs -l service=router -n infra | grep req_0a9c1f2b` to get decision trace.

jonas: Patch plan: small router patch to carry `auth.target_audience = map(original_audience, target_region)` and a guard so relocation will attempt to re-authenticate before sending. Rolling deploy to beta then prod, ETA ~45m.

eli: Customer asked for a credit for the cross-region egress. I'll open a billing ticket with the bot and attach timeline + metrics.

billing-bot: Created chargeback ticket BIL-2025-339 for tenant `acme` with request ids and usage window. Assigned to billing ops.

anna: Can we offer the customer a short-term policy: pin to eu-west for 24h while we finish the patch?

maria: Yes — we can add a per-tenant `pin_region` flag from the console or support API. I'll enable it for `acme` and note the change.

jonas: Action items: (1) maria roll hotfix, (2) enable pin_region for acme, (3) eli file billing credit request, (4) anna update customer with repro + ETA. I'll monitor router traces.

eli: Thanks team. I'll message the customer with the workaround + expected timings. :pray: If the hotfix is slower, we should also consider a temporary fallback policy that preserves token audience.

maria: Patch merged to canary, observing canary traces now. Will post results in 10m.

router-bot: Canary deploy completed on 3/3 canary nodes. No 401s observed for relocated requests in last 5m.

jonas: Seeing reduced relocate rate and queue depth dropping. Closing loop unless new incidents crop up.

eli: Closing on our side — customer acknowledged fix and asked to keep them posted on the billing ticket.
